items.item: The drawings describe one courtyard: fixed elements, canopy, planting and furniture agree wherever they overlap, allowing changes of scale and drawing convention.
Zone names, areas, plant codes, quantities and surface assignments agree with the written analysis and schedule wherever those records appear.
The coordinated design retains the fixed Assembly Court, open lawn, tree protection areas and clear maintenance passage while meeting the learning-route and canopy limits.
Both camera pairs portray the same masterplan geometry and permanent courtyard features; only time-dependent lighting, people and activities change.
Lesson and break scenes support the prescribed pupil distribution and retain clear circulation within the same spatial layout.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Read each drawing against the southwest-origin records: boundary x=0–40 and y=0–30; building x=0–32 and y=24–30; T1=(5,9), T2=(5,13), T3=(5,17), T4=(5,21). Each retained tree must have a 1.8 m protection radius with retained soil or mulch. The east passage occupies x=36–40 and remains unobstructed. Each drawing must dimension its 4 m clear width and the learning route's clearance of at least 1.8 m. Drawing scale and notation may vary; relocated fixed elements, missing protection zones, conflicting dimensions or encroachments fail.

The plan must print the project name and an unambiguous six-zone record: Assembly Court 120 m², Learning Terrace 120 m², Grove 180 m², Open Lawn 140 m², Water Court 120 m² and Circulation 328 m². Labels or a keyed table are acceptable. Values must agree with the source analysis and the fixed client values; omissions, swapped associations or matching an incorrect source value fail.

The masterplan must print all three botanical names exactly as recorded in the analysis and identify Water Court as 120 m² of permeable concrete. Read the planting plan's keyed symbols or planting-group quantities against the schedule: CA means Celtis australis with four retained and two new trees; MT means Myrtus communis 'Tarentina' with 24 shrubs; CD means Carex divulsa with 120 groundcover plants. Grouped planting symbols are acceptable when counts and locations are explicit. Missing names, inconsistent code mappings or incorrect totals fail.

The shade sheet must contain paired 15 July plans using 09:30 azimuth 110°/altitude 38° and 12:30 azimuth 190°/altitude 72°, with azimuth measured clockwise from north. Distinguish canopy and tree shadows and label shaded area inside the fixed Assembly Court rectangle x=10–22, y=10–20 at both times. The noon union of shadow areas inside that court must support at least 90 m² without double-counting overlaps; an unsupported numerical claim fails. Shadow direction and extent must be compatible with the sun inputs and recorded existing and new tree geometry. The masterplan must dimension the coincident 12 m by 10 m canopy envelope, and the section must show clearance of at least 3,000 mm and overall height no greater than 4,500 mm above local ground. Both plan and section must distinguish tree, shrub and groundcover layers. Rendering and hatch styles may vary.

The detail, lesson diagram and lesson views must support a coherent arrangement for six groups of five pupils and one teacher at Learning Terrace. The circulation diagram must show a traversable D1-to-terrace route labelled no more than 35 m. Break evidence must allocate 30 pupils to Assembly Court and 30 to Open Lawn, keeping the 4 m east passage and minimum 1.8 m learning route clear. Natural pose variation and perspective occlusion are acceptable when the paired views and diagram establish the required occupancy; visibly insufficient capacity, contradictory populations or blocked routes fail.

Compare spatial placement, canopy form, planting masses and furniture arrangements with the masterplan and between all views. Each image must carry its correct scene label. People, activities and illumination may change with time, but the built layout must remain identifiable and consistent. Missing labels, switched time labels or unexplained changes to permanent elements fail.

One page must establish the 1,200 m² site, 192 m² existing building and 1,008 m² landscape, and contain six correctly associated zone records. Required areas are 120, 120, 180, 140, 120 and 328 m² for Assembly Court, Learning Terrace, Grove, Open Lawn, Water Court and Circulation respectively. Surface/shade/capacity associations must follow the site records: repaired retained concrete/overhead canopy/60 standing; broom-finished concrete/canopy edge and trees/30 pupils plus teacher; wood-chip mulch/six CA trees/12 seated; retained turf/open sky/30 active; permeable concrete over open-graded aggregate/intermittent trees/12 observing infiltration; retained concrete with flush transitions/mixed exposure/moving pupils and staff. Print Celtis australis, Myrtus communis 'Tarentina' and Carex divulsa. Equivalent descriptive wording is acceptable for surfaces and use, but names, areas and capacities must be accurate.

The plan must make every listed element legible through direct drawing or a clear key, including numbered trees, a usable scale bar and north orientation consistent with the survey. Preserve Assembly Court at x=10–22, y=10–20 and Open Lawn at x=10–24, y=0–10. Place Grove in the west around T1–T4, Learning Terrace east of Assembly Court and south of D1, and Water Court in the southeast west of the maintenance passage. Show connected circulation, an open turf lawn, the six-table teaching arrangement, teacher position and Grove seating. Unfixed zone shapes and graphic conventions may vary; missing elements or contradictions of fixed locations fail.

The section must correspond to the west-to-east cut from (0,17) to (40,17), looking north, and represent the Grove, Assembly Court and eastern courtyard in their plan order. The cut ground is +170 mm throughout; any contextual north–south levels must follow the uniform 1% rise from +0 to +300 mm. Distinguish the three planting layers and dimension canopy heights above local ground. Existing trees and any visible school elevation must respect the recorded 7,000 mm tree height and 6,000 mm building height. Diagrammatic drawing is acceptable; an incorrect cut, invented east–west slope or conflicting elevations fail.

Show six distinct tables with five pupil places per table, a usable teacher position, and an arrival area connected to the learning route. Provide readable seating dimensions that allow the arrangement to be assessed for pupils aged 8–12. Furniture design may vary because no exact seating dimensions are prescribed. Missing dimensions, fewer than 30 pupil places, an absent teacher position or an arrival area occupied by fixed furniture fail.

Locate four retained trees and two new CA trees, 24 MT shrubs and 120 CD groundcover plants through individual symbols or explicitly counted planting groups. Distinguish retained from new trees and coordinate their positions with the masterplan. Locate six teaching tables, a teacher position and 12 Grove seats. Maintenance access must connect the south gate across x=36–40 to the unobstructed east passage. Flexible arrangements of new planting and seats are allowed within the fixed program; unlocated quantities, furniture omissions or blocked access fail.

Read the schedule for ALDER YARD and all six exact zone names with areas of Assembly Court 120 m², Learning Terrace 120 m², Grove 180 m², Open Lawn 140 m², Water Court 120 m² and Circulation 328 m². Include CA—Celtis australis—four retained plus two new; MT—Myrtus communis 'Tarentina'—24; CD—Carex divulsa—120. Surface descriptions must assign repaired retained concrete to Assembly Court, broom-finished concrete to Learning Terrace, wood-chip mulch to Grove, retained turf to Open Lawn, permeable concrete over open-graded aggregate to Water Court and retained concrete with flush transitions to Circulation. Explicitly identify Water Court's 120 m² permeable surface. Table design and descriptive phrasing may vary; incorrect associations, missing construction descriptions or disagreement with the fixed records fail.

Provide clearly distinguishable lesson and break states using paired plans or an unambiguous overlay. Trace the actual walking path from D1, centered at (28,24) with a 2 m door opening, to Learning Terrace. Its labelled distance must be geometrically plausible, no greater than 35 m, and measured along the route rather than through obstacles. Mark the minimum 1.8 m learning clearance and 4 m maintenance clearance. State 30 pupils plus one teacher for the lesson and 30 pupils in each of Assembly Court and Open Lawn for the break. A decorative arrow without measurable routing, ambiguous activity states or contradictory widths fail.

Viewpoint one must retain its camera position and direction between lesson and break, and viewpoint two must do the same while supplying a distinct second view. Both times must depict their corresponding activities and compatible sun conditions. Wherever visible, preserve the school's cream brickwork, teal window frames and flat parapet, together with the retained hard court. Rendering style, people and incidental activity may vary. Camera changes that prevent paired comparison, duplicated viewpoints or altered fixed building appearance fail.

Review the full clip and its playback duration. It must last 10 seconds, begin at D1, move along a spatially coherent route to Learning Terrace and finish with an overview in which the canopy and Grove can both be identified. Compare canopy, planting and furniture with the masterplan throughout. Camera speed and rendering style may vary; a different route, missing ending subjects or changing permanent geometry fail.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation must visibly incorporate identifiable material from every listed source, including all four distinct perspectives. Resizing, cropping and rearranging are acceptable if each source remains recognizable and its relevant content remains readable. Merely naming an earlier deliverable, omitting a source or replacing it with an inconsistent redesign fails.

The presentation must legibly print ALDER YARD and correctly associate the six zone names with their fixed areas: Assembly Court 120 m², Learning Terrace 120 m², Grove 180 m², Open Lawn 140 m², Water Court 120 m² and Circulation 328 m². A readable reused table or drawing satisfies this requirement. Missing records, illegible reuse or agreement with an erroneous analysis value fails.

Find the complete botanical names Celtis australis, Myrtus communis 'Tarentina' and Carex divulsa in readable presentation content and verify their agreement with the analysis. Their placement and typographic treatment may vary. Codes alone, common-name substitutions, omissions or spelling changes fail.

Count at least eight pages and find a readable statement of the Assembly Court target of at least 90 m² geometric shade at 12:30 on 15 July. Presentation depictions must preserve the masterplan's canopy, planting and furniture, and reused perspectives must retain or receive the correct lesson or break labels. Page composition may vary. Fewer pages, an absent or weakened shade target, incorrect scene labels or conflicting spatial depictions fail.

The drawings describe one courtyard: fixed elements, canopy, planting and furniture agree wherever they overlap, allowing changes of scale and drawing convention. Zone names, areas, plant codes, quantities and surface assignments agree with the written analysis and schedule wherever those records appear. The coordinated design retains the fixed Assembly Court, open lawn, tree protection areas and clear maintenance passage while meeting the learning-route and canopy limits.

Both camera pairs portray the same masterplan geometry and permanent courtyard features; only time-dependent lighting, people and activities change. Lesson and break scenes support the prescribed pupil distribution and retain clear circulation within the same spatial layout.
